Money Talk

*   Americans are piling on debt at a rate not seen since the Great Recession, and while some wealth gaps narrowed, people are struggling to make payments. Sounds like a party, right?
*   Hurricane Isaias is currently messing with US oil production in the Gulf, which could make an already tight fuel market (thanks, global conflicts!) even tighter. Fill up now, maybe.
*   Verizon stock just had its worst day since 2002 because Elon Musk's Starlink is coming for the US telecom market. Never bet against the guy with the rockets, apparently.
*   In a move that should surprise exactly no one, OpenAI is now projecting $20 billion *less* in revenue than expected this year. Maybe the AI bubble isn't made of pure unicorn dust after all.
*   The Swiss National Bank bucked the global trend and cut interest rates by half a point to 0.5%, reminding everyone they still do whatever they want. Good for them.

World Lore

*   Turns out Russia might be playing fast and loose with international treaties, specifically one requiring them to report lab worker deaths that could signal an outbreak. Shocker.
*   Nobel Peace Prize went to South African human rights lawyer Navi Pillay, an outspoken advocate for international law. Trump, who openly coveted the prize, did not win. Again.
*   The US is seriously ramping up pressure on Venezuela's former President Nicolás Maduro, adding new torture charges to his existing drug trafficking allegations. Not a great look for him.
*   The EU and China just hammered out a landmark deal that could halve China's hybrid car exports to the bloc, essentially protecting European jobs. Brussels isn't playing around.
*   Fears are growing that clashes between Eritrean and Ethiopian troops in Tigray could spiral into a wider regional conflict. That part of the world really doesn't need more of that.

Tech Tea

*   German regulators finally called BS on Tesla's "Full Self-Driving" name, prompting a rebrand to "Tesla Assisted Driving" in Europe. Because, you know, it's *assisted*, not *full*.
*   Amazon and Microsoft are (finally) ditching NDAs for data center deals with local governments. Turns out, communities don't love secret server farms. Who knew transparency was a thing?
*   Google is teasing a new Fitbit Edge launch next week, hoping to, well, get an "edge" on your health. Still trying to make smartwatches happen.
*   A new startup called LumenUs is automating the paperwork that comes with grief, which sounds genuinely helpful. Less bureaucracy when you're mourning? Sign me up.
*   We're already having to ban users from being "cruel" to AI systems, according to Anthropic. The future is here, and it includes digital empathy.

Creator Szn

*   Top creators are getting smarter, cutting down their brand deal rosters and demanding more from the partners they keep. It's about quality control and market leverage, baby.
*   The WNBA's newest team, the Golden State Valkyries, is navigating how to secure sponsors while staying true to their "mission." A tricky balance between capital and culture.
*   As more creators jump into Hollywood, there's growing concern that typical deal terms could put their intellectual property at serious risk. Read your contracts, kids!
*   Revlon is trying to update its image by tapping into its "heritage" and using current musicians like Teyana Taylor to appeal to a new generation. Old school, new tricks.

Speed Round

*   Ex-Deutsche Bank trader Christian Bittar just had his rate-rigging conviction overturned, becoming the eighth person to clear their name.
*   Germany's manufacturing PMI hit a four-month high, showing a slight pulse in the industrial heart of Europe.
*   The Cook Political Report shifted 18 House races toward Democrats, making the GOP's midterm outlook even more grim.
*   Microsoft is still trying to spark new life into Windows 11, instead of just moving on to Windows 12 already.
*   Elon Musk admitted some of his recent posts on X "went too far," a rare moment of self-reflection from the tech titan.
*   The Department of Homeland Security is facing blowback for publicly attacking a Democratic House candidate.
*   A privacy display on the new Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra lets you hide your screen from prying eyes — finally, no more shoulder-surfing on the commute.
